target: J293 Wi-Fi: PCI 14e4:4425 class 0x028000 (BCM4378), Linux driver brcmfmac, per root's runs/m1-desktop-010/m1-followon-inventory.json. The Bluetooth function 14e4:5f69 (hci_bcm4377) is excluded.

existing_in_puredarwin_e7aa00a.pci_hosts: PDArmPCI and PDEcamPCI match only pci-host-ecam-generic and qcom,pcie-sc8280xp (DesignWare). No Apple PCIe (apcie) host driver.
existing_in_puredarwin_e7aa00a.IO80211Family: Present (30k lines). IO80211Controller : IOEthernetController turns a net80211 ieee80211com into an Ethernet-like interface and answers apple80211 requests. The net80211 tree is an OpenBSD port (net80211/OPENBSD_REVISION c27e9422...).
existing_in_puredarwin_e7aa00a.linuxkpi_80211: fbsdkpi/freebsd/linuxkpi (linux_80211.c, 10k lines) bridges Linux mac80211 SoftMAC drivers onto net80211. It is used by PDFBSDrtw89, PDFBSDrtwn and PDFBSDrun, whose IOKit class is an IO80211Controller.
existing_in_puredarwin_e7aa00a.fullmac_gap: cfg80211 FullMAC support is stubbed: include/net/cfg80211.h has 132 TODO() bodies, including cfg80211_scan_done, cfg80211_inform_bss/_data, cfg80211_disconnected, cfg80211_roamed and cfg80211_ibss_joined, and linuxkpi_80211_wiphy_register is 'TODO: Lots of checks and initialization'. brcmfmac is a cfg80211 FullMAC driver, so it cannot run over this layer without a new cfg80211-to-net80211 bridge.
existing_in_puredarwin_e7aa00a.dart: No Apple DART IOMapper anywhere in the tree.
existing_in_puredarwin_e7aa00a.broadcom: No Broadcom Wi-Fi driver. Only a linuxkpi platform_data/brcmfmac.h header exists.

m1n1_assets_MIT.pcie: src/pcie.c and tunables.c apply ADT apcie-* tunables, port config/LTSSM/PHY and link-up. kboot runs it only on the Linux boot path (kboot.c:6683), but it is also exposed as the proxy command P_PCIE_INIT (proxy.py:703,1212). The current HV path never calls it: no 'pcie:' lines in any guest worker log.

gaps_in_order.gap: Apple PCIe host bring-up and config access
gaps_in_order.options: (a) host calls p.pcie_init() before HV start, so the m1n1 (MIT) tunables and link-up run unchanged; this is a root-owned host change. (b) Port pcie.c logic into a Darwin Apple PCIe host driver. Either way Darwin then needs a host bridge exposing config space and MSI to IOPCIFamily.

Bypass if the PCIe DART supports it for the Wi-Fi stream; otherwise a minimal IOMapper programming the DART page tables. Linux's choice (identity vs translated) is observable read-only through the iommu_group type.
Apple PCIe implements its own MSI to AIC (msi-ranges). It must map onto Darwin IOPCIDevice interrupts through the existing AIC platform driver.

(A, recommended) Native IO80211Controller driver following OpenBSD bwfm/bwfm_pci over the existing OpenBSD net80211 port: a structural fit, BSD/ISC licence, and OpenBSD runs bwfm on Apple silicon. (B) Port brcmfmac (ISC) over LinuxKPI and implement the missing cfg80211 FullMAC bridge (scan cache, connect/disconnect/roam events, key handling): a large new layer. Use Linux brcmfmac as the BCM4378/Apple-specific reference in either case.

gaps_in_order.gap: Firmware, NVRAM, CLM and txcap selection plus Apple quirks
gaps_in_order.detail: Firmware naming from ADT module-instance/antenna-sku/board-type, OTP read, the firmware random-seed requirement, and CLM/txcap download. Blobs are Apple-owned: keep them out of Git and stage them privately in a RAM image only when the user allows.
J293 port power/enable GPIO (pwren) and PERST/CLKREQ sequencing, plus PMGR apcie power domains. Verify against the ADT before any driver writes.

minimal_primary_pins_linux_aurora_6a08a0.note: Paths to verify and acquire by root at the exact commit (not fetched here). GPL files are behavioural references only; ISC brcmfmac files may be adapted with attribution.
optional_reference_large: brcmfmac/cfg80211.c and cfg80211.h (join/scan/key iovar sequences only)

optional_alternative_pins_not_linux: OpenBSD sys/dev/ic/bwfm.c, bwfmvar.h, bwfmreg.h, sys/dev/pci/if_bwfm_pci.c, if_bwfm_pci.h at a pinned revision, if route A is chosen. That is a source decision for root and the user.

allowed: Wi-Fi and its parent bridge under /sys/bus/pci/devices: vendor, device, class, revision, subsystem_vendor, subsystem_device, current/max_link_speed, current/max_link_width, power_state, irq, msi_bus; basename of the driver and iommu_group links; count of msi_irqs entries only
/sys/kernel/iommu_groups/<group of 14e4:4425>/type (identity vs DMA answers the DART bypass question); /sys/class/iommu entry names

/proc/device-tree Wi-Fi and PCIe nodes: compatible, brcm,board-type, apple,antenna-sku, apple,module-instance, reg-names, msi-ranges/iommu-map presence, and the names (not values) of *-gpios properties

Kernel log lines for brcmfmac, apple-pcie and apple-dart, piped through a MAC redactor (sed -E 's/([0-9a-f]{2}:){5}[0-9a-f]{2}/<mac>/Ig') and dropping any line mentioning SSID, connect or wlan association
forbidden: PCI config files or BAR contents
firmware, NVRAM, CLM or txcap file contents (NVRAM can contain macaddr=)

not_claimed: No source acquired, no hardware access, no firmware handling. Bluetooth excluded. Effort and route choice remain root/user decisions.
